page: Microsoft Azure E16s_v3 is an ESv3 family virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance utilizes an Intel Xeon 8370C x86_64 processor with 8 physical cores, 2 threads per core, and a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The CPU features a 50 MB L3 cache and supports AVX and AVX512F instruction sets, alongside AES cryptography and virtualization extensions. Local storage is limited to a 262 GB volume, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance distinction between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core execution is consistently weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-core and memory-bound operations perform at an average level, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also register in the average tier, alongside Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E16s_v3 offers a high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-thread performance. The trade-off lies in the weak single-core processing capabilities, which may bottleneck sequential tasks. Given these characteristics, this server is suited for database operations, memory-intensive web serving, and moderate multi-threaded application hosting, while being less optimal for single-threaded compression or large-scale language model inference.
